title: Normalized Go runtime observation
description: Input to `compare_compute_outputs.py runtime`, which compares it against the pinned v0-celery-baseline capture using the v3-canary-release-proof thresholds. This is NOT the v3 canary observation: that artifact pairs a Celery observation with a Go one and carries a route transport, a route-generation step, and rollback evidence, none of which exist post-cutover. It does carry the same attestation rigour, because a set of in-envelope numbers with no statement of which build, dataset, run, and window produced them is not evidence of anything. The comparator enforces every rule below and refuses the file otherwise.

captured_at.description: UTC instant the capture completed. Must be at or after window.end.

window.description: The observation window. start < end <= captured_at, enforced.

build.description: Which binary produced the observation. Without this the numbers cannot be attributed to anything.

dataset_scope.description: Digest of the dataset the runtime worked over.

run_scope.description: Digest of the run scope the observation covers.

families.description: Task-outcome counts keyed by the v0 baseline's family names. Every family the baseline recorded counts for must appear, or the comparator emits `baseline_family_not_observed`: an operational-health claim over an arbitrary subset is not the claim.

counts.description: All four are required non-negative integers. A missing or malformed count is refused, never read as zero.

profiles.description: Per-profile resource and queue-age measurements. Coverage is required for the union of every profile series the baseline recorded — CPU, memory, and queue age — not only the CPU one. Each value must be finite and non-negative: NaN, an infinity, and a negative all make every threshold comparison False, which is the shape of a pass.
